/-!
# Erdős Problem 972

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/972](https://www.erdosproblems.com/972)
-/

namespace Erdos972

/--
The set of primes `p` such that `Nat.floor (α * p)` is also prime.
-/
def primeSet (α : ℝ) : Set ℕ :=
  {p : ℕ | Nat.Prime p ∧ Nat.Prime ⌊ (α * p) ⌋₊}

/--
**Erdős problem 972.**
Let $\alpha > 1$ be irrational. Are there infinitely many primes $p$
such that $\lfloor p\alpha \rfloor$ is also prime?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_972 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ α > 1, Irrational α → (primeSet α).Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos972

reformulations.difference: The prime-set helper uses natural-number floor rather than ordinary integer floor.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For α > 1 and p : ℕ, αp is nonnegative, so (⌊αp⌋₊ : ℤ) = ⌊pα⌋. Thus membership in primeSet α is equivalent to p being prime and the ordinary integer floor being a natural prime. Infinitude of this set is equivalent to finding such a prime p above every natural-number bound. The membership equivalence and its fully quantified infinitude version were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using the conjecture or sorryAx.
